About SINGU

At SINGU, we’re redefining how the world’s most ambitious real estate companies run their operations. Our mission is to become Europe’s leading platform for managing warehouse, logistics, retail, and multi-site commercial real estate portfolios — empowering our Clients to protect revenue, boost efficiency, and unlock new value across every aspect of their business.

 

Our unified CAFM platform already powers the daily operations of over 250 million m² of real estate worldwide, supporting more than 500,000 professionals. Following our union with the UK’s Micad and Germany’s net-haus, we now help manage 100,000+ buildings across 35+ countries — and we’re just getting started.

 

Backed by a leading growth equity investor, we’re scaling rapidly and partnering with global leaders such as Prologis, ECE, CTP, Hillwood, Logicor, GLP, and Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield. As we continue to grow through strategic acquisitions and bold innovation, we stay true to our core values: adaptability, collaboration, and client focus.

 

If you’re ready to help build Europe’s leading platform for property operations — and make a tangible impact on how the real estate industry works — join SINGU and be part of this transformation.

The Opportunity

SINGU provides property and facilities management technology for organisations operating complex, multi-site estates. Retail is a strategically important market for the business, spanning shopping centres, retail parks, high-street portfolios, supermarkets, hospitality and other distributed consumer environments.

We are seeking an experienced retail property, facilities or operations leader to become SINGU's senior market authority for retail and help build a differentiated, commercially successful position in the sector.

The Retail Market Principal will combine deep industry expertise, executive credibility and market leadership with clear commercial accountability. The role will help SINGU determine where it has the strongest right to win, create access to senior decision-makers, originate strategic opportunities, accelerate priority deals and strengthen SINGU's relevance across the retail property and facilities ecosystem.

This is not a conventional sales, pre-sales, product marketing or communications role. It is a senior, market-facing position for someone who understands retail property and operations at practitioner level and can translate that experience, credibility and network into measurable commercial impact.

Success will be measured not simply through market visibility or activity, but through SINGU's ability to create qualified pipeline, win strategic customers, expand existing relationships and establish a repeatable position within priority retail segments.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12 months, you will have established a clear and credible retail go-to-market strategy, identifying the segments and use cases where SINGU can win disproportionately and building meaningful executive relationships across priority retail accounts.

You will have originated and influenced significant qualified pipeline, contributed demonstrably to both new-logo and expansion revenue, and developed repeatable retail propositions supported by clear customer evidence.

You will also have strengthened SINGU's network of retail customers and advocates, while materially increasing our credibility, relevance and market position within the retail property and facilities sector.

What You Will Own

Retail Market Strategy:

  • Define where SINGU has the strongest right to win across retail.

  • Shape our retail go-to-market strategy, priority segments, use cases and target accounts.

  • Maintain a strong point of view on the operational, regulatory and technology issues shaping retail estates.

  • Translate market insight into clear commercial and product priorities.

Executive Access and Market Development:

  • Build trusted relationships with senior leaders across retail property, facilities, operations, asset management and transformation.

  • Use your network and industry credibility to create access to strategic prospects and originate new opportunities.

  • Represent SINGU in executive forums, customer meetings, roundtables and selected industry events.

  • Build relationships across the wider retail ecosystem, including advisers, FM providers, managing agents and partners.

Strategic Accounts and Commercial Impact:

  • Work with Sales and Customer Success on a focused portfolio of priority retail accounts.

  • Help uncover strategic priorities, strengthen business cases and improve executive engagement.

  • Support selected opportunities where your involvement can materially increase SINGU's probability of winning.

  • Identify expansion opportunities across customers, countries, sites, modules and use cases.

  • Contribute directly to qualified pipeline and revenue growth, without replacing the accountable salesperson.

Customer and Market Insight:

  • Build a strong community of retail customers, advocates and industry influencers.

  • Bring structured market insight into Product, Product Marketing and Commercial Strategy.

  • Identify repeatable customer needs, emerging opportunities and gaps in SINGU's proposition.

  • Help ensure SINGU invests in problems that customers are willing to pay to solve.

Commercial Accountability:

This is not a conventional quota-carrying role, but it has clear commercial accountability. Performance will be measured against:

  • qualified pipeline originated and materially influenced;

  • revenue contribution from strategic retail opportunities;

  • progression and penetration of priority accounts;

  • executive relationships created within target organisations;

  • development of repeatable retail propositions and use cases;

  • customer advocacy and market influence.

Specific commercial targets will be agreed annually.

What We're Looking For:

  • Significant senior experience in retail property, facilities management, estates, operations or asset management.

  • First-hand understanding of complex, multi-site retail estates.

  • Strong credibility and an established network with senior retail stakeholders.

  • Evidence of turning industry relationships and insight into commercial opportunities or strategic outcomes.

  • Strong commercial judgement and the ability to connect operational challenges to financial value, risk and business outcomes.

  • Executive presence, strong communication skills and the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders constructively.

  • The ability to identify what is genuinely scalable and commercially valuable, rather than simply interesting.

  • Experience in software or technology is helpful but not essential; deep retail credibility and commercial instinct matter more.

  • Business-fluent English; Polish and/or German language is an advantage

Package and Progression:

  • Competitive base salary, calibrated to experience and location.

  • Performance-related bonus linked to strategic-account engagement, market influence and measurable commercial contribution.

  • Direct sponsorship from the CRO and access to SINGU's executive leadership.

  • Support from Sales, Marketing, Product Marketing, Product and Pre-Sales.

  • The opportunity to shape SINGU's retail market position across Europe.

  • Progression into broader market leadership, strategic growth or industry-led go-to-market responsibility.

If this role sounds like a good fit, we’d love to hear from you. Apply and help us build technology that supports critical operations every day.

Lightspeed is looking for a strategically minded Strategic Account Manager to develop, engage, and closely support our most important enterprise customers in the hospitality segment over the long term.

In this role, you will act as the primary point of contact for our largest hospitality customers across the UK region. You will be responsible for driving growth, product adoption, and stakeholder management within your portfolio, with the goal of building true business partnerships. You will leverage data, customer feedback, and your SaaS expertise to create value at the enterprise level.

 

What you’ll do

  • Act as the main point of contact for our largest and most strategic hospitality customers

  • Develop and execute strategic account plans to drive growth, retention, and product adoption

  • Proactively work on increasing product usage and ensure Net Revenue Retention (NRR) grows across your portfolio

  • Plan and lead quarterly business reviews and success plans

  • Analyze usage data, go-live milestones, and health scores to identify and mitigate risks early

  • Build strong, trusted relationships with C-level and operational stakeholders, positioning Lightspeed as a long-term strategic partner

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Customer Success, Implementation, and Support teams to deliver an excellent customer experience

  • Collect customer feedback and proactively share it with relevant teams to identify product gaps and optimize the overall customer journey

 

What you bring

  • 3–5+ years of experience in Account Management or Strategic Customer Success within a B2B SaaS environment, ideally with enterprise customers

  • A strong understanding of SaaS metrics (NRR, product adoption, expansion, renewals, churn) and the ability to use them to manage your portfolio

  • A strong sense of ownership; you are hands-on, data-driven, and highly skilled in relationship management

  • Experience managing complex, multi-level stakeholder structures and confidently engaging with C-level, operations, and technical teams

  • Fluent business-level English

  • Experience in the hospitality, POS, or hospitality tech industry is a plus, but not required

     

What’s in it for you?

Come live the Lightspeed Experience…

  • Genuine career growth opportunities based on performance within a company that's continuously expanding

  • Work with highly skilled people who are as passionate about sales & marketing as you are

  • An environment that encourages initiatives and leadership

  • Work in a team big enough for growth but lean enough to make a real impact

  • Fun activities with your teammates & social events throughout the year

  • Opportunity to learn, expand your skill set, forge wonderful relationships and make your mark within the diverse and inclusive Lightspeed culture, a true Canadian tech success story

... and enjoy a range of benefits that’ll keep you happy, healthy and (not) hungry:

  • Lightspeed equity scheme (we are all owners)

  • Health & Wellness Credit- expense up to £400 per year towards your gym membership, yoga classes, a new bike or whatever else you do for your health 

  • Mental Health Support through the Modern Health App - whether it is meditation, coaching or counselling you need - each employee gets access to this platform 

  • People Experience - Our PX benefit allows you to work from pretty much anywhere in the world for 60 days a year 

  • Time off to volunteer and give back to your community

  • Transit benefit if you travel by public transport to the office 

  • Healthy snacks and after-work socials organised by the company

  • Health, Dental and Optical cover

 

We know that people are more than what’s on their CV. If you’re unsure that you have the right profile for the role... hit the ‘Apply’ button and give it a try!

To all recruitment agencies: Lightspeed does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. If we have not directly engaged your company in writing to supply candidates for a specific vacancy, Lightspeed will not be responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

Where to from here?

Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here.

Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. We were founded in 2005, in Montreal’s gay village and our original members were all part of the LGBTQ+ community. The ethos of our business has been about inclusion from the very beginning, and we strive to provide a workplace where everyone belongs.

Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our ADAS Team

Wayve's ADAS engineering teams build the perception and intelligence that power driver assistance in real-world driving. We work end-to-end, from creating high-quality training data, to developing and evaluating CV/3D perception models, to iterating quickly based on performance gaps. The team mixes "online" (on-car, latency/compute constrained) and "offline" (heavier, large-scale data generation) work, with a strong focus on measurable impact and shipping.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Train, debug, and improve computer vision and 3D perception models, iterating based on clear evaluation signals

  • Work across the full ML lifecycle: data, training, evaluation, and iteration

  • Partner with the team to decide what to tackle next, based on where the system is underperforming

  • Build scalable data pipelines, including auto-labelling and pseudo-labelling, to accelerate model development

     

🧩 What you'll be working on:

  • Core ADAS perception capabilities such as detection, classification, and instance segmentation, spanning lanes, objects, traffic signs, and traffic lights

  • End-to-end approaches that let the model act on the world directly, rather than relying on a chain of hand-coded intermediate steps (lane assist without ever explicitly detecting lane lines is the kind of outcome we're after)

  • Online perception that runs fast in-car as part of our production stack

  • Offline perception work using additional inputs not viable for on-road production, including extra sensors like lidar, future frames, maps, and extra compute, to improve data quality and coverage at scale

  • Building the "data flywheel": using offline models and 3D tracking/reconstruction to auto-generate labels and accelerate iteration across perception tasks

     

👤 You should apply if:

  • Built and shipped CV-focused deep learning systems, with strong applied ML engineering rather than research-only work

  • Experience with 3D perception concepts or pipelines, such as LiDAR, multi-view geometry, tracking, or 3D reconstruction

  • Comfortable owning work end-to-end, including evaluation and large-scale dataset generation

  • Enjoy pragmatic problem-solving under real product constraints

  • Excited to improve real-world driving performance through better perception

  • Automotive domain experience is a bonus, but not a blocker if your perception background comes from elsewhere

🌱 Not ticking every box? That's totally okay! If you're passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚗 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve's mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻 — Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

📋 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

  • Competency interviews (programming and system design; 2 hours)

  • Deep-dive technical interviews (Hiring manager/Domain Interview; 1 hour)

  • Final interview: mission & values alignment (1 hour)

We'll always explain the format and work around your availability.

 

What's in it for you (Location dependent):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partner discounts and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

Senior People Partner

Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000

Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function.

THE MOMENT

Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago.

You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them.

This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one.

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT

In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty.

  • Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back.

  • People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding.

  • Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning.

  • CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to.

To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one.

THE ROLE

You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job:

  • Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish.

  • Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs.

  • Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate.

When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day.

WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS

New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today.

Yours

  • The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end.

  • Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding.

  • Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems.

  • Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027):

    • Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago.

    • Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation.

    • Background screening in Zinc.

    • Security clearance coordination.

    • Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting.

    • Our working groups and committees.

  • Once the People Partner joins:

    • A structured handover of the operational core.

    • Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner.

Shared

  • Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that.

  • Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join.

Not yours

  • Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition.

  • The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO.

  • Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO.

THE STACK

  • Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives.

  • Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that.

  • Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for.

  • Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative.

  • Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over.

  • Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done.

  • Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go.

  • Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against.

  • Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook.

  • Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome.

  • Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS

  • You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them.

  • At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you.

  • Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over.

  • You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land.

  • Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point.

  • You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up.

  • The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome.

  • A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to.

  • Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work.

  • Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to.

  • Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards.

  • Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up.

  • Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory.

THE HONEST PART

This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title.

You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows.

This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. It probably is for you if you want to prove you can run this function well enough, top to bottom, that a team gets built around you.

If that sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, let’s talk.

About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the team
The Credit Risk team is part of Airwallex’s Second Line of Defence and helps the company grow responsibly as a global financial platform.
We work at the intersection of credit, FX, and counterparty risk, partnering closely with Product, Sales, Operations, Treasury, Finance, Engineering, Compliance, and Legal to enable commercial growth while protecting Airwallex from financial loss and excessive risk exposure. This is a team for analytical, commercially minded risk leaders who are energized by building scalable frameworks and practical controls across a fast-moving, multi-currency global network.

What you'll do
As a Senior Manager, Credit Risk, you will lead Airwallex's global second-line oversight of credit, FX, and counterparty risk. You will set the risk guardrails that allow the business to grow safely across merchant acquiring, charge cards, FX, treasury, settlement, and banking-partner activities. Reporting to the Senior Director, Financial Risk, you will own the global framework, risk appetite, limits, governance, and portfolio oversight for these risk areas. You will provide independent challenge to first-line decisions and act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders across the business.

This role is based in London.

Responsibilities

  • Credit risk framework and risk appetite: Define, implement, and continuously enhance the global second-line credit risk framework, including policies, risk appetite thresholds, limits, escalation protocols, and governance standards across Airwallex’s products and legal entities.

  • Credit portfolio oversight: Oversee credit exposures across merchant acquiring, charge cards, B2B and commercial activities, FX pre-funding, treasury-related exposures, settlement flows, and other relevant products.

  • Underwriting and limit governance: Review and challenge first-line underwriting strategies, customer and merchant risk policies, credit assessments, limit-setting methodologies, and exception processes. Act as a senior escalation point for complex or high-value credit decisions.

  • FX risk oversight: Establish and monitor appropriate second-line guardrails for FX exposures arising from pre-funding, settlement, customer activity, treasury flows, and other multi-currency activities. Challenge controls, limits, escalation triggers, and risk reporting to ensure exposures remain within approved tolerances.

  • Counterparty risk management: Set and oversee counterparty risk standards for banking partners, payment partners, merchants, customers, and other material counterparties. Establish appropriate exposure limits, concentration thresholds, monitoring requirements, and escalation processes.

  • Portfolio monitoring and early warning indicators: Lead proactive monitoring of credit, FX, and counterparty portfolios, including exposure, concentration, delinquency, default, chargeback, loss, settlement, liquidity-of-counterparty, and other relevant risk indicators. Identify emerging trends and escalate material issues before they become systemic.

  • Loss mitigation and remediation: Review and challenge first-line monitoring, collections, collateral, prefunding, reserves, chargeback, and other mitigation strategies. Ensure deteriorating counterparties, customers, merchants, or exposures are identified and addressed promptly.

  • New products and market expansion: Partner with Product, Engineering, Commercial, Treasury, Finance, and Operations to assess and challenge the risk design of new products, features, markets, currencies, and partner arrangements before launch.

  • Risk approvals and governance: Lead or support risk committee decisions, material risk approvals, limit exceptions, breach assessments, and remediation plans. Ensure decisions are documented clearly and aligned with approved risk appetite.

  • Regulatory and partner engagement: Represent Credit Risk during regulatory examinations, internal and external audits, and reviews with banking and strategic partners. Prepare clear, decision-useful materials for senior management, risk committees, and the Board where appropriate.

Who you are
We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory.



Minimum qualifications

  • 10–15 years of progressively senior experience across credit risk, counterparty risk, FX risk, treasury risk, or related financial risk disciplines within banking, payments, fintech, or another highly regulated financial services environment.

  • Deep experience designing, implementing, and governing second-line credit risk frameworks in a complex, multi-jurisdictional organization.

  • Strong understanding of credit risk identification, measurement, underwriting, limit management, monitoring, mitigation, provisioning, loss recognition, and capital implications.

  • Demonstrated experience managing risk across multiple product lines, such as merchant acquiring, commercial or charge cards, B2B lending, payment processing, FX, treasury, settlement, or banking-partner activities.

  • Practical experience overseeing FX and counterparty risk, including exposure measurement, concentration risk, limits, settlement risk, prefunding, collateral or other mitigants, and escalation governance.

  • Proven ability to challenge first-line decisions and communicate clear risk positions to senior executives, commercial leaders, product and operations teams, banking partners, auditors, and regulators.

Preferred qualifications

  • Advanced degree such as an MBA or Master's in Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or a related field.

  • Professional certification such as FRM, PRM, CFA, or an equivalent qualification.

  • Experience with automated decisioning engines, credit scoring models, portfolio analytics, or alternative data used in underwriting and monitoring.

  • Familiarity with IFRS 9, expected credit loss methodologies, stress testing, or other relevant prudential and accounting frameworks.

  • Strong data literacy and familiarity with SQL, Python, or similar tools used to analyze portfolio, exposure, and loss trends.

  • Experience working in a regulated payments fintech, digital bank, or financial institution with multiple licenses and banking partnerships.

  • Comfort operating in a high-growth environment with evolving priorities and a bias for practical, scalable execution.

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

data.description:
Waracle are looking for a Lead Devops Engineer for an exciting new role joining our world-class digital technology consultancy and home to a diverse, smart, curious and ambitious community of specialists in technology-driven transformation.

We work with ambitious clients to help them solve their biggest business and customer challenges. We help our clients to innovate and create intelligent digital products and services. We thrive on complex  challenges and deliver business-critical IT transformation projects, moving seamlessly from strategy, design and delivery to operations.

This is a Hybrid role working from our Glasgow, Dundee or London office 2 days a week.

As a Lead DevOps Engineer, you’ll serve as an empathetic leader, strategic advisor, and technical authority across our engineering squads. Bringing a broad, generalist mindset across platform engineering and modern infrastructure, you will lead the integration of AI-driven delivery practices, intelligent automation, and Generative AI tooling into everyday workflows. You will define project-level technical architecture, mentor and lift up growing engineers, and nurture a collaborative, psychologically safe environment where everyone feels empowered to innovate. Balancing short-term delivery with long-term maintainability, you will play a key role in de-escalating conflicts, aligning client stakeholders, and driving high-impact technical strategy aligned with human-centric business goals.

Key aspects of the role include

  • Technical Strategy & AI Integration: Defining technical architecture across squads, anticipating system scaling risks, and driving the adoption of modern AI tooling, MLOps, and intelligent automation within cloud environments.

  • Broad Generalist Leadership: Leveraging your breadth of engineering knowledge to bridge gaps between software delivery, platform operations, and data infrastructure, making complex trade-offs clear and explicit for clients.

  • People & Culture: Creating an inclusive, psychologically safe team environment, regularly coaching team members with constructive feedback, and balancing delivery pace with overall team wellbeing.

  • Standards & Compliance: Guiding teams on performance strategies, proactive optimisation, and security standards (such as OWASP, GDPR, SOC2), ensuring responsible AI practices, clean architecture, and secure code execution.

  • Stakeholder Collaboration: Facilitating workshops to discover requirements, managing project scope and expectations, and translating client priorities into actionable technical strategy.

  • Innovation & Influence: Evaluating emerging AI tools and technical approaches through tech spikes, shaping go-to-market strategies for new offerings, driving delivery tooling improvements, and representing Waracle at external tech events.

Research shows that underrepresented groups tend to only apply for roles that they believe they meet 100% of the criteria for. At Waracle, we want to buck that trend! We hire for passion, potential and mindset as much as credentials. If you think you'd be incredible in the role, then apply - even if you don't think you tick every box.


What you'll bring 

  • A versatile, generalist engineering background with broad knowledge across cloud platforms, CI/CD, containerisation, and infrastructure-as-code.

  • Practical exposure to or enthusiasm for integrating Generative AI, AI-assisted development tools, or modern MLOps pipelines into delivery streams.

  • Proven experience guiding technical direction and architecture for cloud and platform solutions.

  • A passion for mentorship, coaching, and creating supportive pathways for engineers at all career stages.

  • Commitment to fostering inclusive, collaborative team dynamics that prioritise wellbeing alongside quality outcomes.

  • Strong understanding of security, accessibility, and compliance standards (OWASP, GDPR, SOC2) in modern cloud architectures.

  • Excellent communication skills with an aptitude for breaking down complex technical concepts for diverse stakeholders.

  • Familiarity with tracking key engineering metrics (such as DORA) to guide continuous, data-informed improvement.

What to expect from our hiring process

1. First Hello: An informal chat with your dedicated Talent Attraction Partner to talk about Waracle, what you want out of your next move, salary, benefits, and office hybrid working model.

2. Talking Impact: A collaborative deep dive into how you solve problems, work with others, and raise the bar, guided by our core values and competency framework.

3. Craft Showcase: A chance to demonstrate your real-world expertise. Depending on the role, this will be a practical presentation.

Your Talent Attraction Partner will be in your corner through every step right up to your Welcome Ritual on day one

Our Benefits

We believe in supporting our team, inside and outside of work. Here's a glimpse of what you can expect:

  • Rest & Recharge: You'll receive 27 days of annual leave, plus 8 bank holidays, totaling 35 days of holiday to unwind and pursue your passions.

  • Financial Future & Security: Plan for retirement with our company-matched 5% pension contribution. For added peace of mind, we also offer a Death in Service benefit, providing 2 x your annual salary for your loved ones.

  • Health & Wellness: Our Medicash Health Cash Plans help cover everyday healthcare costs, complemented by an Employee Assistance Programme for confidential support, and Group Sickness Cover for peace of mind.

  • Flexible Working: We champion hybrid working, providing a home office setup budget to ensure you're comfortable and productive wherever you are.

  • Learning & Development: Invest in yourself with access to Udemy Business and a dedicated learning and development budget for continuous growth.

  • Lifestyle Perks: Make the most of our Cycle to Work Scheme, and enjoy exclusive gym and retail discounts.

  • Family First: Our enhanced parental leave policies include support for fertility journeys, recognising diverse family needs.

  • Community & Connection: We foster a vibrant culture with regular fun meet-ups and lunch on us in the office once a month. You'll also have the opportunity to make a local impact through Spirit of Waracle, our initiative for getting involved in charitable causes locally, building strong team bonds and giving back.

We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all suitably qualified persons regardless of their race, gender, disability, religion/belief, sexual orientation or age.

data.description:
Creandum's edge has always been people: the network, the judgment, the hustle. To sharpen our edge, we need to make everything those people learn compound: every meeting, every diligence process, every founder relationship feeding a shared foundation instead of evaporating into inboxes and individual heads.

You will build and own that foundation: the firm's data platform, the intelligence layer on top of it, and the governance that makes partners willing to trust it with their most sensitive work.

This is a new function, and you are its first hire. You'll start hands-on-keyboard and stay that way for the time being; but you're building an estate the firm will run on, and the mandate grows with what you prove.

You report to the Operating Partner, but work directly and independently with every member of the firm.

We believe different viewpoints drive our growth, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

What you'll own

The data platform. The firm's data architecture end to end: warehouse, ingestion from core systems (CRM, meeting transcripts, documents, email/calendar), entity resolution, and data quality. One person, one company, one deal – consistent across every source. This is foundational; everything else flows from it.

The intelligence layer. Retrieval, search & agent tooling that give everyone's AI real firm context, serving both individual workflows (bottom-up) and firm-wide platforms (top-down). Built for passive compounding: the system gets better as people work and as models improve, without depending on anyone's discipline.

Access, trust, and AI risk. The access model as structural enforcement, not instructions: who sees what, with identity, provenance, and audit. Sensitive fund and partner data protected to a standard the partnership will trust, plus the AI-specific risk judgment (injection containment, egress, tool guardrails) for everything the function ships, in collaboration with legal/regulatory counsel.

Technology strategy and the tool estate. Accountability for whether the firm's tools are the right ones: evaluation, integration, and replacement of the systems and data sources the firm runs on, in close partnership with the stakeholders who use them. Buy when buying is better; build when building is better. You have the mandate to choose, and then execute on your decision. Make sure security, compliance and budget are part of the equation.

What you'll deliver

First 6 months. A complete map of the firm's data and systems. The foundational data platform stood up. Two or three lightweight tools shipped that visibly improve how a team works. A clear, prioritized 12–18 month roadmap, authored by you and agreed with the partnership.

By 12 months. V1 of the firm's shared intelligence layer live and in daily use. The diligence process made genuinely multiplayer; firm knowledge and meeting history informing live deals instead of sitting unused. Measurable adoption, reported honestly, with failures killed as quickly as the wins are shipped.

Beyond. The roadmap is yours to define. Candidates for the frontier: productizing how the firm wins deals, network intelligence that answers "who do we know" in seconds, platform tools founders can self-serve, and operational automation across finance, events, and admin.

How you'll work

  • Builder first. You ship personally. This is not a role for someone who wants a team of ten doing the building.

  • Co-creation, not solo genius. Stakeholders across the firm (investment, platform, marketing, operations, etc.) steer, test, and tune what you build. Within a year, everyone at the firm should be able to point at something they had a hand in shaping.

  • Product discipline. Prototype, validate with real users, kill what doesn't get adopted. Usage is the metric; expect and budget for churn.

  • Scale deliberately. You start solo. As the foundation proves out, you'll orchestrate internal or external build resources and potentially grow the function. You are prepared to identify, leverage and lead exceptional talent to help achieve results.

Who you are

  • You've shipped a real data or AI product end to end (pipelines, retrieval, and the product surface) and people actually used it.

  • Deep, hands-on command of data architecture, warehousing, and governance. Fluent with embeddings, retrieval, and agents that act, not just answer.

  • You treat access control and provenance as product features, not compliance chores.

  • Low ego, high agency, energized by a blank page. Excited to tackle the unglamorous work (entity resolution, data hygiene, permissions) that everything depends on.

  • You can sit with an investor, an EA, and a founder in the same week and design for all of them. Venture experience isn't required, but you'll need to earn a front-line view of the work fast.

  • You can say "no" and "not yet" to smart, senior people and make them glad you did.

What this role is not

  • Not IT operations: endpoint, device & office infrastructure are handled by our managed IT partner.

  • Not reg compliance: policy & DORA workstreams are owned by legal, with your input on anything AI.

  • Not a reporting function: you build systems that answer questions, not dashboards on request.

Why this role

You'll have a blank page, real budget influence, direct partnership access, and a firm small enough that what you build touches everyone within weeks. The firms that figure this out will compound differently from the ones that don't. This is the seat where that happens.

data.description:
Your mission

You own the direction of our formal verification business. Our managers keep delivery predictable. You decide what the organisation becomes.

You report to the CEO and are a member of the executive leadership team. You carry the FV consulting business as a whole — where it goes, how it performs, who leads it — and you answer for it. You will not solve verification problems, and you will rarely run a project or an account yourself. Concretely, you own:

  • Direction. The roadmap for FV consulting. Which capabilities, markets and problem domains we pursue, and what we decline.
  • Customers. You are the face of LUBIS EDA to our key accounts and at executive level. You open the doors your managers cannot, and you carry the conversations that decide a long-term relationship.
  • Organisation. Structure, standards, playbooks, talent pipelines, and the career framework in practice. You keep improving how we work, and you decide when a new technology — AI among them — changes the way we deliver.
  • Leaders. Our Verification Managers report to you. You hire them, develop them, and grow the bench behind them. This is the main measure of the role.
  • Quality. Holding the quality bar under commercial pressure. Our entire positioning depends on it.
  • Product interface. What our engineers learn on customer projects is the best input our software roadmap gets.


Your profile

You have developed leaders, not "only" engineers. You have set direction where there was no precedent, made the calls, and carried an organisation with you. You build systems that outlast your attention.

You need credibility in formal verification. Not to overrule your senior engineers. You need it to make the calls only you can make: is a capability gap real, is a quality standard achievable at the price we quote, does a bet on a new formal domain hold.

YOUR EXPERIENCE

  • 12+ years in semiconductor verification, EDA or adjacent engineering services.
  • 5+ years in leadership, including managers reporting to you.
  • Fluent in formal methods and their trade-offs. Credible with a customer’s engineering leadership and on a conference stage.
  • You know how technical services are priced and defended on quality rather than volume.
  • Nice-to-have: you have scaled a technical organisation past start-up stage, where the systems had to be built.


Why us?

LUBIS is growing, and we’re looking for a Head of Formal Verification.

This is one of those roles where you don’t just join an organisation. You help build it.

Our formal sign-off business is growing. Our customers are getting bigger. So are our ambitions. We’re looking for someone who wants real ownership of what comes next: how we develop our people, how we deliver outstanding projects, how we work with our customers, and what world-class technical consulting at LUBIS should look like.

You’ll work directly with our leadership team. You’ll have the freedom to shape structures and standards. You’ll build an organisation around some of the strongest formal verification expertise in the market.

We’re not looking for someone to maintain what already exists. We’re looking for someone who gets excited about making it better, bigger and more professional.

If you want a leadership role with real influence, and the chance to build something you’ll be proud of, come build it with us.

Vous cherchez un environnement professionnel stimulant basé sur l'autonomie et la confiance ?

Pennylane vous offre l'opportunité de grandir au sein d'une entreprise en pleine croissance.

Ici, votre expertise contribuera directement à aider les entrepreneurs à reprendre le contrôle de leurs finances. Découvrez un lieu où vos compétences seront valorisées et où vous pourrez façonner l'avenir de la gestion financière.

 

Notre vision

Notre ambition est de devenir le logiciel de pilotage financier préféré des PMEs européennes.

Nous aidons les entrepreneurs à se débarrasser des tâches chronophages liées à la comptabilité et à la finance, tout en leur donnant accès à des informations financières clés pour les aider à prendre les meilleures décisions pour leur entreprise.

Parallèlement, nous aidons les cabinets d'expertise-comptable, en leur permettant de passer moins de temps sur des tâches redondantes et répétitives, et plus de temps sur la partie conseil et accompagnement de leurs clients.

 

À propos de Pennylane

Pennylane est une des FinTech à la plus forte croissance en France, et souhaite bientôt adresser le marché européen.

 

En 6 ans d'existence, nous sommes parvenus à :

💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant

💰 Lever un total de 400 millions d'euros, auprès d'investisseurs de renom, dont Sequoïa, le fonds phare de la Silicon Valley, connu pour avoir soutenu Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal et bien d'autres à leur début

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Passer de 7 cofondateurs à une équipe de 1200 collaborateurs, avec une note moyenne de 4,9/5 sur Glassdoor et 94% des évaluateurs Glassdoor qui recommanderaient PL à leurs proches!

🌍 Construire une équipe internationale composée de collaborateurs issus de 25 pays différents, avec une culture du télétravail très flexible

🤝 Gagner la confiance de milliers d'utilisateurs et obtenir d'excellents retours

🚀 Déjà plus de 1 500,000 TPE/PME et plus de 7000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France !

Why is this role important for Pennylane?

Pennylane is building Pennylane Financial Services (PFS), a newly created regulated subsidiary applying for ACPR authorisations as a payment institution and a financing company.

This step is foundational to delivering a comprehensive financial-services product for our clients, on a model that is robust, scalable, and supervision-ready.

From day one, the ACPR will expect PFS to demonstrate clear security governance, effective oversight of critical dependencies, and credible evidence of operational resilience - with a strong security-by-design approach.

How will you contribute to the project?

You will own PFS’s security governance and overall security and resilience policy, under the direct supervision of the Chief Compliance and Risk Officer.

Your contribution is to design a risk and control framework that is proportionate to PFS’s activity and regulatory expectations, and to ensure PFS can evidence "security by design" through auditable, inspection-ready artefacts.

In practice, this includes:

  • Policy alignment: ensure consistency between PFS and Pennylane SAS security policies, leveraging the group framework where appropriate while prioritising PFS’s regulatory obligations.

  • Security by design: translate requirements into actionable standards and control expectations, embedded into product and engineering delivery.

  • Operational resilience: shape incident-management and continuity expectations, ensure they are testable, and drive evidence of effective execution.

  • Oversight of key stakeholders: establish effective oversight of Pennylane SAS and key providers, with clear expectations, monitoring and remediation follow-through.

This is a role for a technically credible security leader with strategic judgement - with the technical depth to challenge architectures, controls and evidence, and the seniority to own governance and executive reporting.

What will your day-to-day responsibilities be?

  • Own PFS Information Security policy: define, maintain and continuously improve PFS security governance, standards and policy set.

  • Manage the PFS risk and control framework: maintain the security risk taxonomy, control objectives, key risks/KRIs, escalation thresholds, and evidence expectations.

  • Embed security-by-design into the Product/Tech development cycle: leverage Pennylane SAS policies and existing ways of working where applicable, ensuring PFS security requirements and regulatory obligations are reflected in the delivery lifecycle, change process and go/no-go decisions, without creating unnecessary process overhead.

  • Ensure operational resilience / continuity / testing: define resilience requirements and ensure end-to-end testing and exercises produce usable evidence and tracked remediation.

  • Manage outsourcing arrangements and audits: oversee security aspects of outsourcing arrangements (intragroup and third parties), ensure auditability and follow through on findings and remediation.

  • Provide executive-level reporting: deliver clear, decision-oriented reporting on information-security posture, incidents, resilience testing and remediation to PFS management and the Supervisory Board.

KPIs / signals:

  • Policy & standards effectiveness: evidence of adoption (e.g., security requirements consistently reflected in delivery artefacts for material initiatives) and reduction of recurring “same class” issues over time.

  • Core security KRIs (within risk appetite): a small set of measurable KRIs with thresholds and owners (e.g., critical vulnerability exposure, privileged-access exceptions, key third-party risks), tracked and escalated when outside appetite.

  • Resilience testing KPIs: tests/exercises executed vs plan; % of high-severity findings remediated within agreed timelines; retest completion for failed scenarios.

  • Incident classification & remediation tracking: consistent classification, timely escalation, and tracked remediation to closure (including post-incident action closure rate).

  • Audit follow-up tracking: audit findings/actions ageing, % overdue by severity, and executive visibility on the top overdue items.

  • Threat & vulnerability landscape monitoring: regular review of the external threat/vulnerability landscape and its concrete impact on PFS priorities (what changes in controls, monitoring, or roadmap).

Ramp-up / expectations during the probation period:

  • Establish the initial PFS security governance baseline (policy set, decision rights, reporting cadence).

  • Propose and align a first set of PFS security KRIs and risk appetite thresholds (with owners and escalation path).

  • Produce a first resilience testing plan (what is tested, frequency, evidence expected) and agree success criteria.

  • Put in place an incident classification approach and a remediation tracking routine that is audit-ready.

Profile we are looking for

Must-have

  • Fintech and/or Banking experience

  • Strong experience in information security, technology risk, cyber-risk or security assurance, with ownership of complex topics.

  • Proven ability to design and run security governance and a risk/control framework with audit-ready evidence.

  • Experience working with outsourced / third-party / group-shared technology services while retaining accountability.

  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including executive-level reporting.

  • Professional fluency in French and English.

Nice to have

  • Operational resilience experience, including DORA-aligned practices (incident management, continuity, testing, third-party oversight).

  • Knowledge of payment and authentication topics (SCA, strong authentication and account recovery patterns).

  • Exposure to PCI DSS scope and payment-card security concepts.

  • Payment fraud and transaction-monitoring familiarity (fraud patterns, controls, investigations, and collaboration with Fraud/AML stakeholders).

data.title: CISO

data.description:
Are you looking to have an impact on the daily life of millions of entrepreneurs in France (and tomorrow in Europe)?

Are you looking for a work environment that values trust, proactivity, and autonomy?

Then Pennylane is the right place for you !

 

Our vision

We aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones).

We help entrepreneurs rid themselves of time-consuming tasks related to accounting and finance while providing them with access to key financial information to assist in making the best decisions for their business.

 

About us

Pennylane is one of the fastest growing Fintechs in France (and soon to be in Europe!)

 

In 5 years of existence, we’ve managed to :

💻 Make ourselves known as a groundbreaking accounting and financial software for small businesses and their accountants

💰 Raise a total of €400 millions, including from Sequoia, the famous fund from the Silicon Valley who invested early in companies like Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal and much more...

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Grow from 7 cofounders to 1000 happy Pennylaners : we’re now recognized as one of the greatest places to work in France (and also remotely), with a 4.6/5 rating on Glassdoor.

🌍 Build an international environment with more than 25 nationalities, with a strong remote-friendly culture, where 30% of the employees are already working from all parts of Europe

🤝 Earn the trust of thousands of customers and accounting firms and obtain outstanding ratings

🚀 Already more than 1 300,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and over 6000 accounting firms use Pennylane in France!


Why is this role important for Pennylane?

Pennylane is building Pennylane Financial Services (PFS), a newly created regulated subsidiary applying for ACPR authorisations as a payment institution and a financing company.

From day one of licensing, PFS must be able to operate in full regulatory compliance - not only through policies, but through reliable execution: clear ownership, predictable reporting routines, auditable evidence, and effective coordination across Operations, Finance/Accounting and Compliance & Risk.

This role is critical to organise and run that regulatory function, with the ambition to progressively consolidate regulatory reporting ownership within PFS.

How will you contribute to the project?

You will help build and operate the regulatory office of Pennylane Financial Services, working across Compliance & Risk, Finance, Legal, Operations and Technology.

Your initial priority will be to turn PFS’s regulatory requirements into a reliable operating framework: a complete obligations inventory, clear ownership, an integrated regulatory calendar, and effective controls over regulatory reporting and evidence.

In practice, you will:

  • maintain the authoritative inventory of PFS’s regulatory obligations;

  • coordinate the regulatory-reporting portfolio and directly produce selected returns;

  • establish clear responsibilities, reporting controls and escalation paths across contributing functions;

  • support supervisory responses and commitment tracking from day one;

  • coordinate regulatory change with Compliance, Legal and the relevant subject-matter owners; and

  • support regulatory governance through clear reporting, decision tracking and follow-through.

You will not replace the specialist accountability of Finance, the MLRO, Legal, Risk or Operations. Your role will be to make their contributions converge into a controlled, timely and inspection-ready regulatory process.

As PFS grows, you will help shape and evolve its regulatory operating model and governance arrangements.

What will your day-to-day responsibilities be?

  • Maintain the regulatory-obligations inventory: keep a complete and current view of PFS’s recurring and event-driven obligations, with clear owners, deadlines, controls, approval routes and evidence requirements.

  • Run the integrated regulatory calendar: coordinate contributors, dependencies and review milestones across Compliance & Risk, Finance, Legal, Operations and Technology, escalating delivery risks before deadlines are affected.

  • Coordinate regulatory reporting: oversee the end-to-end reporting portfolio and directly prepare selected returns, while ensuring specialist functions retain accountability for their underlying judgements and data.

  • Establish reporting controls: document and operate source-to-report lineage, reconciliations, variance analysis, maker-checker review, sign-offs, submission evidence, correction procedures and backup arrangements.

  • Coordinate data-quality remediation: document reporting-data issues, assign them to the accountable function, monitor resolution and escalate overdue or recurring problems.

  • Support supervisory responses and commitment tracking: maintain a reliable record of requests, responses and commitments; coordinate contributions and evidence under the direction of the ACPR relationship owner; and escalate delivery issues to PFS management.

  • Coordinate regulatory change: work with Compliance, Legal and relevant subject-matter owners to translate new requirements into impact assessments, accountable owners, implementation plans and evidence.

  • Support regulatory governance: prepare concise status reporting, maintain decision and action tracking, and ensure regulatory matters reach the appropriate management or governance forum.

  • Improve tools and processes: define practical requirements for workflow, evidence storage, reporting production and regulatory remittance, reducing manual effort without weakening controls.

Profile we are looking for

Must-have

  • Meaningful experience in a regulated financial environment, in one or more areas such as regulatory reporting, regulatory operations, prudential reporting, compliance, risk, finance, internal control or regulatory advisory.

  • Strong understanding of reporting controls and data quality, including reconciliations, source-to-report traceability, review and approval controls, exception management and auditable evidence.

  • Sound regulatory judgement: ability to understand a requirement, identify its practical implications, recognise when specialist Legal or Compliance input is needed, and translate conclusions into ownership, processes and controls.

  • Strong execution discipline, with a demonstrated ability to coordinate recurring deliverables, manage interdependencies and meet fixed deadlines reliably.

  • Ability to work effectively across Finance, Legal, Compliance, Risk, Operations and Technology, while preserving clear accountability between functions.

  • Ability to build structured and durable ways of working—including registers, calendars, procedures, templates and knowledge bases—in an evolving environment.

  • Clear and concise written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain issues, assumptions and required decisions to senior stakeholders.

  • Professional fluency in French and English.

Nice-to-have

  • Experience with ACPR reporting, supervisory interactions or the French regulatory environment.

  • Experience in a payment institution, electronic-money institution, financing company, bank, regulated fintech, supervisory authority or specialist advisory firm.

  • Exposure to more than one regulatory domain, such as payments, prudential reporting, statistical reporting, AML-CFT, fraud, incidents or financing activities.

  • Experience coordinating regulatory change, supervisory requests, inspections or remediation commitments.

  • Familiarity with regulatory-remittance tools, reporting-data lineage, workflow automation or evidence-management solutions.

  • Experience building or materially improving a regulatory framework in a new entity, licensing programme or operating-model transformation.

Recruitment Process

1. Interview with Simon (30-45 min), Senior Recruiter

2. Interview with Laurent (1h), Compliance&Risk Director

3. Case Study with two Finance or Legal representative (1h)

4. Team fit with two interviewers (30 min)

5. Last round with Maxime and Felix (45 min)

What do we do to make your work life easier

🌴 Wherever you are based, you will get 25 vacations days paid by Pennylane

💵 You’ll have a competitive compensation package

📈 You'll get company shares to enjoy a piece of the success story you're building with us

🏡 You’ll have a budget to turn your home into a more comfortable workspace, as well as a monthly allowance to work from a coworking space whenever you feel like it

⛹️ Through our partner Gymlib, you’ll have access to 8000 fitness spaces in Europe and more than 300 activities related to wellness

💻 You’ll get the latest Apple equipment

🏢 Depending on the teams and the requirements of the position - you'll be able to work remotely from your country of residence, as long as it is in Europe and within a maximum time difference of two hours from the CET time zone

🎉 We are committed to regularly coming together for company events such as Tech Days (which bring remote Pennylaners together every 3 months) or our annual company seminar, fostering significant moments of cohesion for everyone.

 

If you are based in France, you will have a French contract following French regulation on top of the additional perks : 6 to 12 RTT, 5 weeks PTOs, lunch credits (Swile), Alan Blue healthcare cover and regular events in cities where Pennylaners are mostly presents (Lyon, Bordeaux, Nantes…)

We're working on providing those last advantages to our people based outside of France as well, but it can be quite more complex depending on different countries.

 

Who are we looking for ?

To thrive at Pennylane, you need :

-To speak English (level is assessed and appreciated according to the department you’re applying to)

-To be energized by an ever-shifting work environment

-To be highly collaborative (within your team or other stakeholders)

-Sufficiently experienced to prioritize business-led actions on your day to day activity

 

We know that some people are less likely to apply than others, if they don’t feel like they meet the full list of criteria.

If you’re hesitating, we encourage you to apply : who knows, it might be the start of a meaningful and long-lasting collaboration.

 

Important information for candidates

Recruitment scam attempts are on the rise. We invite you to remain vigilant during your exchanges.

Applications through official channels only : apply exclusively through our job postings published on our official platforms (career site, official partner pages).

Always verify the sender's email address: our communications are sent from professional email addresses with the domains ----- or ----- style="min-height:1.5em">We will never ask you for payment or financial information

(bank details, payment for an interview, equipment purchases, etc.) as part of the recruitment process. If such a request is made to you, it is fraudulent. We invite you to not respond and to report it to us immediately.

 

We also want to emphasize that we fully embrace diversity, equity and inclusion and that we’re doing our best to create a safe and inclusive environment.

We are committed to providing an equal employment opportunity regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, disabilities, or any other traits that make you who you are. If anything, diversity makes us a more fun place to work at.

Vos missions

·         Négocier et contractualiser les accords fonciers et commerciaux.

Votre profil

·         Formation Bac+5 : école de commerce, master en aménagement du territoire, urbanisme ou droit rural.

Ce que NOVAR vous offre

Chez Novar, nous ne vous proposons pas seulement un emploi – nous vous invitons à rejoindre une véritable aventure. Vous travaillerez dans un environnement entrepreneurial et innovant, où l’énergie est au cœur de tout – au sens propre comme au sens figuré. Aux côtés de professionnels passionnés, vous contribuerez concrètement à la mise en œuvre de systèmes énergétiques durables. Et qu’est-ce que cela vous apporte ?

💰 Un salaire attractif, compris entre 48 060 € et 62 383 €, en fonction de votre expérience et de votre parcours.

🌴 Une prime vacances.
🩺 Mutuelle famille financée à 50% 
🚗 Une voiture de fonction.
🏠 Un mode de travail flexible et hybride – dans nos bureaux modernes ou confortablement depuis chez vous.
📚 Des opportunités de développement professionnel dans le domaine du stockage d’énergie par batteries (BESS).
🏆 Un voyage collectif annuel avec l’ensemble du groupe Novar, une expérience inoubliable – travailler dur et célébrer ensemble.

À propos de Novar – Nous façonnons l’avenir énergétique de l’Europe

Chez Novar, nous croyons que l’avenir de l’énergie est vert – et nous le concrétisons. Depuis notre création en 2014 aux Pays-Bas, nous sommes devenus un acteur majeur du développement et de l’exploitation de grandes installations d’énergies renouvelables. Avec plus de 150 collaborateurs engagés et 800 MWc de capacité installée, nous faisons avancer la transition énergétique à pleine vitesse. 

 

Ce qui a commencé par des centrales solaires au sol est devenu une entreprise énergétique complète. Aujourd’hui, nous développons et fournissons de l’énergie solaire, du stockage par batteries, du solaire thermique, de l’hydrogène, des réseaux intelligents et bien plus encore. Nous couvrons toute la chaîne de valeur – du développement et de la construction à la gestion de l’énergie et à l’innovation. 

 

Depuis 2024 nous étendons nos activités au-delà de notre marché d’origine, avec une présence en Suède, en Allemagne et en France. Notre objectif est ambitieux : développer 4 gigawatts de systèmes énergétiques verts d’ici 2030. Chez Novar, vous rejoindrez une équipe internationale en pleine croissance, animée par la volonté de faire la différence. Nous ne construisons pas seulement des projets énergétiques – nous façonnons les systèmes énergétiques de demain.
